comparison: Both strongly support the core finding of AA-LTP with synchronous stimulation (C4, C23-C30). OpenEval emphasizes appropriate controls and statistical analysis. Peer reviewers acknowledge this as a key finding with confidence in the conclusions, noting the unique potentiation versus depression pattern.

Both address rundown effects (C28-C30). OpenEval considers rundown adequately controlled and supports the claims. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about rundown's impact on interpretability, though acknowledge appropriate controls were used. This represents a key area of divergence in confidence level.

Both address the associative nature of plasticity (C35-C38). OpenEval finds strong support for associative requirement with co-activation. Peer reviewers also accept the associative nature, noting that individual pathway stimulation alone produces no LTP. Full agreement on this aspect.

Both address the core AA-LTP finding (C4, C23-C24), but peer reviewers raise significant concerns about contradiction with prior literature showing PF-LTP under various conditions. OpenEval finds claims supported without noting this literature conflict. Major divergence on contextualization within existing literature.

Both address AA-LTP and associative stimulation (C4, C35-C37). OpenEval supports the claims based on experimental evidence. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about whether AA synapses were actually stimulated, citing lack of anatomical verification. Critical methodological concern raised by peers but not by OpenEval.

Perfect claim overlap (C5, C39-C43) on timing-dependent plasticity. Both evaluations support the findings. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative data and bidirectional control. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge timing and order-dependent effects. Complete agreement on this aspect.

Both address mGluR1 and NMDAR involvement (C6-C7, C53-C56). OpenEval finds strong support from pharmacological experiments. Peer reviewers also acknowledge receptor involvement but note that which cell types express these receptors and their specific contributions remain unclear. Partial agreement with peers wanting more mechanistic detail.

Perfect claim overlap (C61-C63) on GABAAR involvement. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of statistical significance (p=0.1) and high variability. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, acknowledging GABAAR involvement though describing it as partial or modulatory. Divergence in confidence based on statistical threshold interpretation.

Perfect claim overlap (C64-C67) on sparse PF control experiment. Both evaluations support the findings. OpenEval emphasizes this as critical control showing synaptic properties, not distribution, determine plasticity. Peer reviewers accept the control without challenge. Complete agreement.

Both address PPR analysis and postsynaptic mechanisms (C31-C34). OpenEval supports the claims while noting this is indirect evidence. Peer reviewers explicitly accept the PPR-based conclusion of postsynaptic plasticity without challenge. Agreement on interpretation despite OpenEval noting limitations.
